decision: Treat issue #3388 as a staged implementation and make the Rust API path work before expanding every SDK YAML helper
why: The issue spans several SDKs and many public messages; a compiling vertical slice exposes the schema and ownership decisions for review
result: open

decision: Supersede the placeholder timestamp in the first row with this actual start time
why: The log is append-only, so the incorrect placeholder remains visible and this row corrects it
result: corrected

decision: Base the implementation branch on current origin/main after PR #3334 merged
why: The public proto work should extend the canonical authored schema crate instead of recreating its parser
result: branch feat/3388-public-policy-proto/pimlock created

decision: Keep documented policy choices as validated strings and use message presence for MCP versions
why: This preserves current YAML vocabulary and SDK forward compatibility while fixing the repeated-field presence gap
result: public package compiles; schema tests pass

decision: Retain the #3334 Serde DTO as a temporary compatibility codec around the generated message
why: A working public API boundary can land before the generic-tree-only codec rewrite without changing the wire contract
result: generated-to-YAML round trip works

decision: Persist public policy in SandboxSpec but keep revision rows, compute-driver messages, and supervisor configuration internal
why: The public contract must exclude derived authority while enforcement still needs normalized provenance-bearing state
result: production Rust workspace compiles across the public/internal boundary

decision: Reuse the public endpoint and binary messages in ProviderProfile and lower them through openshell-policy at the gateway boundary
why: Provider profiles author the same policy language and should not maintain a second generated schema
result: provider profile API uses openshell.policy.v1 while its YAML DTO remains provider-owned

decision: Do not add generated proto validation annotations in this slice
why: Most security invariants are contextual across protocol, endpoint, provider attachment, and effective-policy composition; generated field checks would supplement but cannot replace the existing validators
result: intrinsic schema validation remains in openshell-policy-schema and contextual validation remains in openshell-policy/gateway

decision: Align public field numbers with the existing runtime messages wherever semantics and wire types match
why: Although the new major version permits source breaks, retaining compatible tags reduces persisted-record and mixed-client migration risk; intentionally reshaped JSON-RPC and MCP submessages remain explicit conversion boundaries
result: common endpoint and middleware fields retain their historical wire numbers; internal authority tags are reserved

decision: Treat raw generated SDK availability as complete for the vertical slice and record curated/test-fixture migration as follow-up
why: Rust production crates compile and Go/TypeScript generate the public package, but legacy Rust test fixtures and Go curated converters still assume runtime messages
result: known incomplete migration remains visible and blocks declaring the whole issue complete

decision: Preserve historical endpoint and middleware tag numbers for semantically identical public fields
why: The API review found that aesthetic renumbering would turn an avoidable source break into a wire and persistence break; MCP and JSON-RPC remain intentionally reshaped where authored presence cannot use the runtime representation
result: matching fields now retain tags and runtime-only authority tags 18 and 26 are reserved

decision: Lower edited public draft rules before encoding the internal DraftChunkRecord
why: The independent audit found EditDraftChunk persisted openshell.policy.v1 bytes that later code decodes as openshell.sandbox.v1; MCP and recursive matcher layouts are not wire-compatible
result: public edit input now crosses the same checked lowering boundary before internal persistence

decision: Make provider-profile protobuf conversion fallible at untrusted ingress
why: A malformed public endpoint must produce an import diagnostic instead of panicking inside the gateway
result: server import uses try_from_proto; the infallible wrapper is restricted to trusted validated values

decision: Generate the public policy package for Python and rewrite its relative import
why: The API binding imports policy_pb2 after openshell.proto begins referencing the public package
result: manual Python generation completes with package-local imports

decision: Reject middleware integers that cannot round-trip exactly through google.protobuf.Value
why: Struct stores numbers as f64, so accepting a larger YAML integer would silently change policy semantics
result: 9007199254740993 is rejected by a regression test

decision: Preserve present-empty MCP versions so validation can reject them
why: Only omission selects the pinned default; an explicitly empty authored list is invalid and must not normalize to a default
result: omitted versions materialize the default while present-empty public versions fail conversion

decision: Require a clean gateway database for this new-major prototype unless a one-time migration is added
why: Persisted SandboxSpec and StoredProviderProfile now embed public messages whose MCP, matcher, and JSON-RPC layouts are not wire-compatible with old records
result: policy revision rows remain compatible; mixed-version rollout and old embedded records are explicitly unsupported

decision: Lower standalone authored rules through a complete public SandboxPolicy
why: The rule-only adapter previously bypassed document-level intrinsic validation, allowing present-empty MCP versions to be normalized before rejection
result: provider imports and draft edits now apply the same authored validation as complete policy updates

decision: Open a draft PR with production Rust checks green and fixture/curated-SDK failures explicit
why: The implementation is a usable architecture prototype, but converting 174 Rust test fixtures and the curated Go model is separate mechanical work that should not be hidden behind a green claim
evidence: cargo check --workspace; cargo clippy --workspace --lib --bins; cargo test --workspace --no-run; mise run go:ci
result: production Rust and focused boundary tests pass; all-target Rust and curated Go remain draft blockers

decision: Supersede the temporary YAML compatibility codec with strict descriptor-driven protobuf-shaped YAML
why: The team chose one language-neutral authored shape and accepted breaking scalar and shorthand spellings
result: bounded YAML decodes directly through the openshell.policy.v1 descriptor without a rewrite shim

decision: Supersede present-empty MCP versions rejection; omitted null and empty select the same pinned default
why: Proto3 repeated fields do not preserve presence and policy YAML now follows protobuf semantics
result: MCP versions is a repeated string and all absence-equivalent shapes materialize the default

decision: Supersede the clean-database requirement by preserving internal durable sandbox and provider-profile wire shapes
why: The public schema belongs at API and file boundaries; durable gateway state remains an internal implementation detail
result: existing database rows decode without a one-time migration while API reads project to public messages

decision: Remove runtime-only authority fields from the curated Go policy model and generate openshell.policy.v1 bindings
why: SDK callers must not be able to author advisor or provider-derived provenance
result: Go API models the public matcher oneofs recursive parameters tool matcher and MCP body limit

decision: Give scalar port and repeated ports spellings one internal policy identity
why: The public proto exposes both historical fields, while hashes, history deduplication, and size enforcement require equivalent authored policies to lower identically
result: validated policies materialize ports and retain the first effective port in the scalar field

decision: Measure policy size after lowering the public message to its canonical internal representation
why: Compact public protobuf spellings must not bypass the policy limit when defaults and normalized fields expand internally
result: boundary-size tests cover omitted empty and explicit MCP defaults at and above the limit

decision: Treat provider-profile protobuf messages from every source as fallible authored input
why: External interceptors and stored user profiles can supply malformed policy fields; catalog construction must report a failed precondition instead of panicking
result: malformed MCP versions remain unchanged through normalization and fail catalog validation

decision: Keep main's explicit L7 append target and express its binaries and rule payloads with the public policy proto
why: The target closes an authorization ambiguity and belongs to the external UpdateConfig contract alongside its authored payload
result: CLI and Go SDK send public target binaries and public allow or deny rules; the gateway lowers them before merge

decision: Persist provider_attachment_epoch in the gateway-private sandbox wire message
why: Main added the field to SandboxSpec and dropping it during public-to-internal storage conversion would break provider readiness generation tracking
result: old rows decode with an empty epoch and new rows round-trip it without exposing internal policy fields

decision: Reject YAML mapping keys that are not strings before ProtoJSON decoding
why: Noyalib intentionally stringifies scalar mapping keys, which would otherwise turn numeric, boolean, or null keys into different authored data
result: bounded parsing is followed by a CST key check; quoted scalar-like strings remain valid

decision: Apply the 256 KiB canonical policy limit to every mutation path
why: Create already enforced the limit, but full replacement, global replacement, and incremental merge could persist oversized policies
result: all replacement and merge paths reject oversized canonical policies with INVALID_ARGUMENT and a request-specific field path

decision: Keep an invalid baked image policy fail-closed and repairable through the gateway
why: Silently substituting a fallback would weaken image restrictions, while terminating immediately would prevent an operator repair before first activation
result: the supervisor reports rejected admission, does not launch, and accepts a later valid gateway policy
